title: Dental focus searches and their significance in medicine
summary:
Patients scheduled for cancer therapy, organ transplants, or certain medications are often referred to a dentist beforehand. The aim is to check for hidden infections in the mouth—so-called “infection foci”—which could lead to serious complications during treatment. These foci might include untreated root infections or gum disease.

This study analyzes patient records from 2008 to 2024 to understand whether such oral infection foci actually impact treatment outcomes, such as causing poor wound healing or jawbone problems. Dental X-rays and clinical findings will be compared with the medical progress of each patient. The goal is to determine how important it is to detect and treat these dental problems early—before major medical therapies begin.
conditions: Disorder of teeth and supporting structures, unspecified

interventions.name:
Patients in whom a dental focus was identified during the dental infection screening. These patients receive appropriate treatment (focus elimination) if indicated.

Complete clinical examination (dental status, oral mucosa, salivary glands)
six-point periodontal probing per tooth
evaluation of
Patients in whom no odontogenic focus was found and no dental intervention was necessary.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who underwent dental infection screening at the Department of Conservative Dentistry and Periodontology at LMU Munich between July 12, 2008, and December 1, 2024.
A clear medical indication for the screening, such as before:
Radiation or chemotherapy,
Anti-resorptive or anti-angiogenic therapy,
Organ transplantation,
Or systemic inflammatory conditions of unclear origin.
Availability of complete clinical and radiological documentation.
Unique KAS-ID enabling linkage to clinical outcome data.
Exclusion criteria:
Incomplete clinical records (e.g., missing radiographs or periodontal documentation).
Unclear or undocumented indication for screening.
No possibility for pseudonymized data linkage (e.g., missing KAS-ID).
Patients not referred for infection screening in the context of relevant medical therapy.
